statements.verbatim_passage: This study demonstrates the need for planning, public health, and emergency management perspectives to consider heat resilience through the mitigation and management of heat risk. We found that the drive-through POD model of mass COVID-19 vaccination increases personal heat exposure for unshaded tasks, increasing heat risk for unacclimated workers and volunteers.
statements.passage_as_proposed: This study demonstrates the need for planning, public health, and emergency management perspectives to consider heat resilience through the mitigation and management of heat risk. We found that the drive-through POD model of mass COVID-19 vaccination increases personal heat exposure for unshaded tasks, increasing heat risk for unacclimated workers and volunteers.

time.quote: Data collection occurred during the peak heat hours from 12:00 PM to 5:00 PM at UArizona on March 31, 2021, at Banner South on April 1, 2021, and at TMC on April 2, 2021.

proposal.statement: Extreme heat increases personal heat exposure for unshaded tasks at outdoor vaccination sites, raising heat risk for unacclimated workers and volunteers.
proposal.passage: This study demonstrates the need for planning, public health, and emergency management perspectives to consider heat resilience through the mitigation and management of heat risk. We found that the drive-through POD model of mass COVID-19 vaccination increases personal heat exposure for unshaded tasks, increasing heat risk for unacclimated workers and volunteers.
proposal.time_quote: Data collection occurred during the peak heat hours from 12:00 PM to 5:00 PM at UArizona on March 31, 2021, at Banner South on April 1, 2021, and at TMC on April 2, 2021.
proposal.impact_mechanism: high ambient temperatures and solar radiation increase WBGT in full‑sun locations
proposal.impact_outcome: workers and volunteers experience higher heat stress, requiring mitigation measures

statements.verbatim_passage: WBGT were on average 8°F (4.4°C) higher in full sun, consistent with the general rule that full sun adds up to an additional 15°F (8.3°C) of personal heat exposure [26].

proposal.statement: Full‑sun exposure can raise wet‑bulb globe temperature by about 8 °F (4.4 °C) compared with shaded areas, indicating substantially higher personal heat stress in sunlit zones.
proposal.passage: WBGT were on average 8°F (4.4°C) higher in full sun, consistent with the general rule that full sun adds up to an additional 15°F (8.3°C) of personal heat exposure [26].
proposal.impact_mechanism: solar radiation directly raises ambient temperature and WBGT in sun‑exposed work zones
proposal.impact_outcome: increased risk of heat‑related illness for staff and volunteers

statements.passage_as_proposed: A single evaporative cooler in a tent (Location 6 UArizona; Location 6 TMC). Even with instrumentation within a yard of the direct breeze, ambient temperatures were only lowered by 1°F (0.6°C) to 2°F (1.2°C) and less than 1°F (0.6°C) of WBGT.

time.quote: Data collection occurred during the peak heat hours from 12:00 PM to 5:00 PM at ... April 2, 2021.

proposal.statement: Evaporative cooling devices can lower ambient temperature by 1–2 °F (0.6–1.2 °C) and WBGT by less than 1 °F (0.6 °C) in small shaded areas, providing modest heat‑stress reduction.
proposal.passage: A single evaporative cooler in a tent (Location 6 UArizona; Location 6 TMC). Even with instrumentation within a yard of the direct breeze, ambient temperatures were only lowered by 1°F (0.6°C) to 2°F (1.2°C) and less than 1°F (0.6°C) of WBGT.
proposal.time_quote: Data collection occurred during the peak heat hours from 12:00 PM to 5:00 PM at ... April 2, 2021.
proposal.impact_mechanism: evaporative coolers reduce ambient temperature and WBGT in shaded tents
proposal.impact_outcome: modest decrease in heat stress for personnel in those areas

statements.verbatim_passage: The safety threshold was exceeded at all three sites by the highest vehicle surface temperatures, at UArizona up to 158.7°F (70.4°C); at Banner South up to 160°F (71.1°C); and at TMC up to 170.9°F (77.2°C).
statements.passage_as_proposed: The safety threshold was exceeded at all three sites by the highest vehicle surface temperatures, at UArizona up to 158.7°F (70.4°C); at Banner South up to 160°F (71.1°C); and at TMC up to 170.9°F (77.2°C).

time.quote: Data collection occurred during the peak heat hours ... April 2, 2021.

proposal.statement: High vehicle surface temperatures can exceed safety thresholds, reaching up to 170 °F (77 °C), which may pose burn hazards for personnel handling vehicles.
proposal.passage: The safety threshold was exceeded at all three sites by the highest vehicle surface temperatures, at UArizona up to 158.7°F (70.4°C); at Banner South up to 160°F (71.1°C); and at TMC up to 170.9°F (77.2°C).
proposal.time_quote: Data collection occurred during the peak heat hours ... April 2, 2021.
proposal.impact_mechanism: radiant heat from vehicles raises surface temperatures
proposal.impact_outcome: potential for burns or heat injury to staff handling vehicles

statements.verbatim_passage: We recorded enough ambient temperatures above the reported maximums to suggest that management based on the projected high temperature may underestimate heat risk.
statements.passage_as_proposed: We recorded enough ambient temperatures above the reported maximums to suggest that management based on the projected high temperature may underestimate heat risk.

proposal.statement: Ambient temperature forecasts can underestimate on‑site heat risk, as measured temperatures frequently exceeded reported daily maximums.
